facts.statement: Cladodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Ctenacanthidae.
facts.quote: Cladodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fishes in the family Ctenacanthidae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cladodus have been discovered in Scotland, Australia, and the United States.
facts.quote: Fossils of Cladodus have been found in Barkip, Scotland, Bundock and Laurel Formations, Australia and in the Pitkin Formation (Carboniferous period) in Arkansas, United States.

facts.statement: Cladodus possessed teeth designed to snag prey and swallow it whole rather than cutting it into pieces.
facts.quote: As the name implies, they are a type of cladodont, primitive sharks with teeth designed to snag fish and swallow them whole, instead of sawing off chunks to swallow.

facts.statement: Cladodus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Cladodus lived between 379 and 227.3 million years ago, from the Frasnian to the Carnian periods.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Carnian (379 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Remains consisting of a braincase and a tooth of Cladodus have been found in the Clackmannan Group of Scotland.
facts.quote: Remains (braincase and a tooth) have been found in Scotland (Clackmannan Group).

facts.statement: The teeth of Cladodus range in length from 2.2 to 90 millimeters.
The species Cladodus gailensis was described by Feichtinger and colleagues in 2021.
